builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: LIRA: A More Interpretable Dynamic Loss-Informed Rank Allocation for Low-Rank Adaptation
summary: LIRA replaces fixed-rank or heuristically reallocated LoRA with periodic rank reallocation scored by a second-order estimate of the local loss perturbation from recent LoRA-factor movements, while keeping standard (A,B) adapters and matched rank budgets. It costs periodic rank-scoring and reallocation overhead during training, plus implementation complexity beyond stock LoRA, though the Trajectory EMA variant reduces estimation cost relative to the Fisher-based variant. It can fail if the second-order approximation misestimates layer importance on tasks or architectures beyond RoBERTa-base GLUE, and its reported gains are validated only at that small scale.
rationale: The method is deployable on a single 24 GB GPU for fine-tuning workloads, but its quality gains are demonstrated only on GLUE-scale tasks and require validation on the reader's specific models before production adoption.
technique: Loss-informed dynamic rank allocation for LoRA

claims.statement: LIRA replaces fixed-rank or heuristically reallocated LoRA with periodic rank reallocation scored by a second-order estimate of the local loss perturbation from recent LoRA-factor movements, while keeping standard (A,B) adapters and matched rank budgets. It costs periodic rank-scoring and reallocation overhead during training, plus implementation complexity beyond stock LoRA, though the Trajectory EMA variant reduces estimation cost relative to the Fisher-based variant. It can fail if the second-order approximation misestimates layer importance on tasks or architectures beyond RoBERTa-base GLUE, and its reported gains are validated only at that small scale.
On RoBERTa-base GLUE under the La-LoRA/LoRA protocol, LIRA outperforms uniform-LoRA and adaptive-rank baselines; no multiplicative factor is reported.
